messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the detailed report.

This looks like a familiar error I’ve seen with RStudio when using datadr.  I have no idea the cause and we have filed these errors with RStudio, but these are always red herrings.  Even though there is an error, it has something to do with the RStudio IDE, and there was not an error in the execution of your code.  The error can be ignored completely.  Your output object should be fine.  take a look at data.2008 and see if it looks in tact.  If it doesn't, try intializing a ddf:

ddf(hdfsConn(loc="/user/tessera-user/data-out-01”)

The data should be there.

If not, I’m wrong and we’ll have to investigate further.

messages.subject: RHIPE and MapReduce v1
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Does RHIPE still support MapReduce v1?

The older tar.gz files had 'mr1' and 'mr2' in their file names to indicate different Hadoop versions. However, from RHIPE 0.75.1.3 onwards, the naming scheme is different; it is now 'cdh5' and 'hadoop-2'.

I am encountering problem with RHIPE 0.75.1.5 when using it on a Hadoop MapReduce v1 cluster running on Red Hat Linux.

The specific error is:
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError:
org.apache.hadoop.mapreduce.Job.addCacheFile(Ljava/net/URI;)V

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: RHIPE and MapReduce v1
messages.body_plain:
RHIPE v0.75 is mr2 only.  Although they are supposed to be compatible, there were too many nuanced differences between mr1 and mr2 that we had to break into separate branches.  You can get RHIPE that runs with mr1 in the v0.74 branch.  It is not under active development, but has been used quite extensively so it should work.  You can get prepackaged travels at http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipebin/.

Ryan

messages.subject: No display in Trelliscope
messages.body_plain:
I am running Debian Wheezy (7.8) on two different systems (laptop and server).   I am unable to get Trelliscope to display any information using your sample scripts for Housing Data and Census data.  These systems are running R 3.1.2.

I have also run your script emr-3.2.1 and successfully installed Rstudio on an AWS cluster.  The individual graphics in your sample scripts work in both R and Rstudio on both local and AWS machines.

Running view() launches the browser with an unpopulated trelliscope. I have also tried opening up the permissions on the display directories.

Stand-alone shiny examples work on all my machines.  I have turned off all browser add-ons.

I would like to include Trelliscope in an upcoming demo I am doing, but I can't find any documentation on the Tessera site about requirements/settings for Trelliscope to understand what might be causing the problem.

Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Ryan W

If it doesn’t, please let us know and we’ll help you figure out what might be causing the problem.

Thanks!

Ryan
